title: Machine-learning-guided closed-loop synthesis experimentally realizes unreported dye molecules
summary: A closed-loop molecular discovery platform combined machine-learning property prediction, automated synthesis and characterization, and iterative model updates to explore dye-like molecules. In the published Science abstract, the team reports experimentally realizing 294 previously unreported molecules across three design–make–test–analyze cycles on four rarely reported scaffolds, while also identifying six top-performing molecules in a second case study using pre-existing chemical-space examples.
ai_technology: Autonomous molecular-discovery platform integrating generative and property-prediction machine-learning models, Bayesian optimization, and synthesis-planning software with automated chemical synthesis and characterization
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: In the published Science abstract, the team reports experimentally realizing 294 previously unreported molecules across three design–make–test–analyze cycles on four rarely reported scaffolds, while also identifying six top-performing molecules in a second case study using pre-existing chemical-space examples.
evidence.unknown: This is molecular discovery in dye-like chemical systems, not a validated drug or biological effect. The 294 number is from the published Science abstract; an earlier ChemRxiv preprint describes 312 unreported molecules, so version-specific counts differ and the published figure is used here. The measurements addressed absorption wavelength, lipophilicity and photo-oxidative stability; no environmental, toxicological or commercial benefit is claimed. Primary-source abstract and author-lab description checked; independent replication not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Generative ML proposed candidate dye-like structures; property-prediction models ranked molecules against absorption, lipophilicity, and photo-oxidative-stability targets; automated multi-step synthesis and measurements generated training data for model retraining and the next cycles. The closed-loop process converted model-guided suggestions into synthesized and characterized compounds.
